Registered\nin `src/Kraken.jl` (exported by `using Kraken`).\n\"\"\"\nfunction assemble_poisson_embedded_from_fvfd(eb, f;\n                                             outer_bc::Symbol=:neumann,\n                                             embedded_bc::Symbol=:neumann,\n                                             outer_dirichlet::Function=_fvfd_poisson_zero_dirichlet,\n                                             embedded_dirichlet::Function=_fvfd_poisson_zero_dirichlet)\n    vol_frac, face_frac_x, face_frac_y = fractions_from_fvfd(eb)\n    Nx, Ny = size(vol_frac)\n    Nx == Ny ||\n        throw(ArgumentError(\"assemble_poisson_embedded_from_fvfd requires a square grid, got (\$Nx, \$Ny)\"))\n    return assemble_poisson_embedded(\n        Nx, face_frac_x, face_frac_y, vol_frac, f;\n        outer_bc, embedded_bc, outer_dirichlet, embedded_dirichlet,\n    )\nend\n```"), (name = :fractions_from_fvfd, signature = "function fractions_from_fvfd(eb)", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    fractions_from_fvfd(eb) -> (vol_frac, face_frac_x, face_frac_y)\n\nConvert a duck-typed FVFD embedded boundary object with `cell_fraction`,\n`west_fraction`, `east_fraction`, `south_fraction`, and `north_fraction`\nfields into the open-fraction arrays consumed by `assemble_poisson_embedded`.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    fractions_from_fvfd(eb) -> (vol_frac, face_frac_x, face_frac_y)\n\nConvert a duck-typed FVFD embedded boundary object with `cell_fraction`,\n`west_fraction`, `east_fraction`, `south_fraction`, and `north_fraction`\nfields into the open-fraction arrays consumed by `assemble_poisson_embedded`.\n\"\"\"\nfunction fractions_from_fvfd(eb)\n    Nx, Ny = size(eb.cell_fraction)\n    Nx > 0 && Ny > 0 ||\n        throw(ArgumentError(\"cell_fraction must have positive dimensions, got (\$Nx, \$Ny)\"))\n    _fvfd_poisson_check_size(:west_fraction, eb.west_fraction, (Nx, Ny))\n    _fvfd_poisson_check_size(:east_fraction, eb.east_fraction, (Nx, Ny))\n    _fvfd_poisson_check_size(:south_fraction, eb.south_fraction, (Nx, Ny))\n    _fvfd_poisson_check_size(:north_fraction, eb.north_fraction, (Nx, Ny))\n\n    vol_frac = Matrix{Float64}(undef, Nx, Ny)\n    face_frac_x = Matrix{Float64}(undef, Nx + 1, Ny)\n    face_frac_y = Matrix{Float64}(undef, Nx, Ny + 1)\n\n    @inbounds for j in 1:Ny, i in 1:Nx\n        vol_frac[i, j] = _fvfd_poisson_fraction(eb.cell_fraction[i, j], :cell_fraction, i, j)\n    end\n\n    @inbounds for j in 1:Ny\n        face_frac_x[1, j] = _fvfd_poisson_fraction(eb.west_fraction[1, j], :west_fraction, 1, j)\n        for i in 1:Nx\n            face_frac_x[i + 1, j] =\n                _fvfd_poisson_fraction(eb.east_fraction[i, j], :east_fraction, i, j)\n        end\n        for i in 1:(Nx - 1)\n            _fvfd_poisson_check_face_match(\n                eb.east_fraction[i, j], eb.west_fraction[i + 1, j],\n                :east_fraction, :west_fraction, i, j, i + 1, j,\n            )\n        end\n    end\n\n    @inbounds for i in 1:Nx\n        face_frac_y[i, 1] =\n            _fvfd_poisson_fraction(eb.south_fraction[i, 1], :south_fraction, i, 1)\n        for j in 1:Ny\n            face_frac_y[i, j + 1] =\n                _fvfd_poisson_fraction(eb.north_fraction[i, j], :north_fraction, i, j)\n        end\n        for j in 1:(Ny - 1)\n            _fvfd_poisson_check_face_match(\n                eb.north_fraction[i, j], eb.south_fraction[i, j + 1],\n                :north_fraction, :south_fraction, i, j, i, j + 1,\n            )\n        end\n    end\n\n    return vol_frac, face_frac_x, face_frac_y\nend\n```"), (name = :solve_poisson_mg, signature = "function solve_poisson_mg(f, N::Integer;", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    solve_poisson_mg(f, N; bc=:dirichlet, backend=CPUBackendTag(), tol=1e-10,\n                     maxcycles=50, nu1=2, nu2=2, ncoarse=50, smoother=:rbgs,\n                     verbose=false)\n        -> (u, ncycles, resid_history)\n\nSolve `-∇²u = f` on the unit square with a regular `N x N` cell-centred grid via\na matrix-free geometric multigrid V-cycle.\n\nArguments\n  `f`  either a `Function (x,y) -> f(x,y)` sampled at cell centres, or an\n       `N x N` array already holding the RHS at cell centres.\n  `N`  grid size (square). Should be a power-of-two multiple of the coarsest grid\n       (default coarsest >= 4) so the hierarchy halves cleanly.\n\nKeywords\n  `bc`        `:dirichlet` (homogeneous; inhomogeneous data must be folded into\n              `f` by the caller, as in poisson.jl) or `:neumann` (all-Neumann,\n              singular — handled by zero-mean projection / pin).\n  `backend`   `CPUBackendTag()` (default) or `CUDABackendTag()`.\n  `backend_ka` optional explicit KA backend (e.g. `CUDABackend()`); overrides the\n              tag translation. Lets a GPU job pass its live backend directly.\n  `atype`     device array type for allocation (default `Array{Float64}`; pass\n              `CuArray{Float64}` for GPU).\n  `tol`       relative-residual stopping tolerance.\n  `maxcycles` cap on V-cycles.\n  `nu1,nu2`   pre/post smoothing sweeps.\n  `ncoarse`   coarsest-grid smoothing sweeps.\n  `smoother`  `:rbgs` (default, red-black Gauss-Seidel) or `:jacobi` (weighted).\n  `sigma`     Helmholtz shift: solves `(σI - ∇²)u = f` on the unit square\n              (σ has units 1/length² in unit-square coordinates). Default 0\n              recovers the plain Poisson operator. A positive σ makes the\n              operator non-singular and strongly diagonally dominant — used by\n              the cavity momentum solve (under-relaxed/pseudo-transient\n              predictor). With σ>0 the Neumann case is NOT projected to zero\n              mean (the shift removes the constant nullspace).\n  `u0`        optional `N x N` initial guess (warm start); default zero start.\n              Lets a SIMPLE loop reuse the previous solution to cut V-cycles.\n  `fixed_cycles`  when > 0, run EXACTLY this many V-cycles with NO residual-norm\n              computation at all (no `fnorm`, no per-cycle relative residual):\n              zero host reductions/syncs and a STATIC kernel-launch sequence\n              (CUDA-graph-capturable later). `tol`/`maxcycles` are ignored.\n              For `:neumann` the RHS is assumed discretely zero-mean (true for\n              a conservative face divergence) and the per-level zero-mean\n              projections are SKIPPED: the V-cycle commutes with constant\n              shifts, so the result only differs by an additive constant,\n              which the caller must gauge away. Default 0 = tolerance-driven\n              behavior (unchanged).\n  `hier`      optional pre-built `MGHierarchy` (from `build_mg_hierarchy(N,\n              atype)`) to reuse across repeated solves of the same size —\n              avoids re-allocating the full level stack per call (a per-\n              iteration allocation in SIMPLE loops). All level arrays are\n              fully (re)initialized here, so reuse is value-identical.\n  `mixed_precision`  when true, each V-cycle becomes a Float64 defect-correction\n              step whose inner V-cycle runs entirely in Float32 (see\n              `_mg_mixed_cycle!`): residual in F64, error solve in F32,\n              correction added back in F64. Opt-in; default `false` keeps the\n              all-Float64 path bit-identical. Composes with `fixed_cycles`\n              (the mixed cycle is also a static, reduction-free launch\n              sequence). The returned solution stays Float64.\n  `hier_f32`  optional pre-built Float32 `MGHierarchy` (from\n              `build_mg_hierarchy(N, _mg_eltype_variant(atype, Float32))`) for\n              `mixed_precision=true`; reuse it across repeated solves exactly\n              like `hier`. Ignored when `mixed_precision=false`.\n\nReturns the solution `u` (N x N device array), the number of V-cycles performed,\nand the relative-residual history (one entry per cycle, on the host; EMPTY when\n`fixed_cycles > 0`).\n\nValidation & performance receipts\n  * MMS second order, V-cycle count flat vs N (the multigrid hallmark), parity\n    vs the assembled CHOLMOD solver, and the singular Neumann variant:\n    `test/analytical/poisson_mg_mms.jl`.\n  * GPU (issue #8, Aqua A100): V-cycle counts stay flat at 10–13 from 16k to\n    16M DOF (O(N) per cycle, O(1) cycles) and MG-GPU reaches ~43x MG-CPU at\n    16M DOF, saturating the device (peak 99% util) where cuDSS idles —\n    `benchmarks/krk/inc_ns/poisson_mg_gpu_bench.jl`,\n    `benchmarks/results/poisson_mg_gpu_aqua_a100.md`. For moderate-N 2D steady\n    problems the factorize-once cuDSS path still wins per-solve (different\n    regimes; see the results note).\n  * GPU↔CPU parity at machine epsilon (‖Δ‖∞ ~1e-14, same source via the KA\n    backend swap).\n\nRegistered in `src/Kraken.jl` (exported by `using Kraken`); the file remains\nstandalone-include-able (its guard pulls in `linear_solve.jl` for the backend\ntags when needed).\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    solve_poisson_mg(f, N; bc=:dirichlet, backend=CPUBackendTag(), tol=1e-10,\n                     maxcycles=50, nu1=2, nu2=2, ncoarse=50, smoother=:rbgs,\n                     verbose=false)\n        -> (u, ncycles, resid_history)\n\nSolve `-∇²u = f` on the unit square with a regular `N x N` cell-centred grid via\na matrix-free geometric multigrid V-cycle.\n\nArguments\n  `f`  either a `Function (x,y) -> f(x,y)` sampled at cell centres, or an\n       `N x N` array already holding the RHS at cell centres.\n  `N`  grid size (square). Should be a power-of-two multiple of the coarsest grid\n       (default coarsest >= 4) so the hierarchy halves cleanly.\n\nKeywords\n  `bc`        `:dirichlet` (homogeneous; inhomogeneous data must be folded into\n              `f` by the caller, as in poisson.jl) or `:neumann` (all-Neumann,\n              singular — handled by zero-mean projection / pin).\n  `backend`   `CPUBackendTag()` (default) or `CUDABackendTag()`.\n  `backend_ka` optional explicit KA backend (e.g. `CUDABackend()`); overrides the\n              tag translation. Lets a GPU job pass its live backend directly.\n  `atype`     device array type for allocation (default `Array{Float64}`; pass\n              `CuArray{Float64}` for GPU).\n  `tol`       relative-residual stopping tolerance.\n  `maxcycles` cap on V-cycles.\n  `nu1,nu2`   pre/post smoothing sweeps.\n  `ncoarse`   coarsest-grid smoothing sweeps.\n  `smoother`  `:rbgs` (default, red-black Gauss-Seidel) or `:jacobi` (weighted).\n  `sigma`     Helmholtz shift: solves `(σI - ∇²)u = f` on the unit square\n              (σ has units 1/length² in unit-square coordinates). Default 0\n              recovers the plain Poisson operator. A positive σ makes the\n              operator non-singular and strongly diagonally dominant — used by\n              the cavity momentum solve (under-relaxed/pseudo-transient\n              predictor). With σ>0 the Neumann case is NOT projected to zero\n              mean (the shift removes the constant nullspace).\n  `u0`        optional `N x N` initial guess (warm start); default zero start.\n              Lets a SIMPLE loop reuse the previous solution to cut V-cycles.\n  `fixed_cycles`  when > 0, run EXACTLY this many V-cycles with NO residual-norm\n              computation at all (no `fnorm`, no per-cycle relative residual):\n              zero host reductions/syncs and a STATIC kernel-launch sequence\n              (CUDA-graph-capturable later). `tol`/`maxcycles` are ignored.\n              For `:neumann` the RHS is assumed discretely zero-mean (true for\n              a conservative face divergence) and the per-level zero-mean\n              projections are SKIPPED: the V-cycle commutes with constant\n              shifts, so the result only differs by an additive constant,\n              which the caller must gauge away. Default 0 = tolerance-driven\n              behavior (unchanged).\n  `hier`      optional pre-built `MGHierarchy` (from `build_mg_hierarchy(N,\n              atype)`) to reuse across repeated solves of the same size —\n              avoids re-allocating the full level stack per call (a per-\n              iteration allocation in SIMPLE loops). All level arrays are\n              fully (re)initialized here, so reuse is value-identical.\n  `mixed_precision`  when true, each V-cycle becomes a Float64 defect-correction\n              step whose inner V-cycle runs entirely in Float32 (see\n              `_mg_mixed_cycle!`): residual in F64, error solve in F32,\n              correction added back in F64. Opt-in; default `false` keeps the\n              all-Float64 path bit-identical. Composes with `fixed_cycles`\n              (the mixed cycle is also a static, reduction-free launch\n              sequence). The returned solution stays Float64.\n  `hier_f32`  optional pre-built Float32 `MGHierarchy` (from\n              `build_mg_hierarchy(N, _mg_eltype_variant(atype, Float32))`) for\n              `mixed_precision=true`; reuse it across repeated solves exactly\n              like `hier`. Ignored when `mixed_precision=false`.\n\nReturns the solution `u` (N x N device array), the number of V-cycles performed,\nand the relative-residual history (one entry per cycle, on the host; EMPTY when\n`fixed_cycles > 0`).\n\nValidation & performance receipts\n  * MMS second order, V-cycle count flat vs N (the multigrid hallmark), parity\n    vs the assembled CHOLMOD solver, and the singular Neumann variant:\n    `test/analytical/poisson_mg_mms.jl`.\n  * GPU (issue #8, Aqua A100): V-cycle counts stay flat at 10–13 from 16k to\n    16M DOF (O(N) per cycle, O(1) cycles) and MG-GPU reaches ~43x MG-CPU at\n    16M DOF, saturating the device (peak 99% util) where cuDSS idles —\n    `benchmarks/krk/inc_ns/poisson_mg_gpu_bench.jl`,\n    `benchmarks/results/poisson_mg_gpu_aqua_a100.md`. For moderate-N 2D steady\n    problems the factorize-once cuDSS path still wins per-solve (different\n    regimes; see the results note).\n  * GPU↔CPU parity at machine epsilon (‖Δ‖∞ ~1e-14, same source via the KA\n    backend swap).\n\nRegistered in `src/Kraken.jl` (exported by `using Kraken`); the file remains\nstandalone-include-able (its guard pulls in `linear_solve.jl` for the backend\ntags when needed).\n\"\"\"\nfunction solve_poisson_mg(f, N::Integer;\n                          bc::Symbol = :dirichlet,\n                          backend::LinearSolveBackend = CPUBackendTag(),\n                          backend_ka = _mg_ka_backend(backend),\n                          atype::Type{<:AbstractArray} = Array{Float64},\n                          tol::Real = 1e-10,\n                          maxcycles::Integer = 50,\n                          nu1::Integer = 2,\n                          nu2::Integer = 2,\n                          ncoarse::Integer = 50,\n                          smoother::Symbol = :rbgs,\n                          min_size::Integer = 4,\n                          sigma::Real = 0.0,\n                          u0 = nothing,\n                          fixed_cycles::Integer = 0,\n                          hier::Union{Nothing, MGHierarchy} = nothing,\n                          mixed_precision::Bool = false,\n                          hier_f32::Union{Nothing, MGHierarchy} = nothing,\n                          verbose::Bool = false)\n    N = Int(N)\n    kab = backend_ka\n    sig = Float64(sigma)\n    nfixed = Int(fixed_cycles)\n\n    bctag = bc === :dirichlet ? MG_BC_DIRICHLET :\n            bc === :neumann   ? MG_BC_NEUMANN   :\n            throw(ArgumentError(\"bc must be :dirichlet or :neumann\"))\n    bcs = (bctag, bctag, bctag, bctag)  # (west, east, south, north)\n    neumann_pin = bc === :neumann\n\n    if hier === nothing\n        hier = build_mg_hierarchy(N, atype; min_size = min_size)\n    else\n        hier.sizes[1] == N || throw(ArgumentError(\"reused hierarchy is sized \$(hier.sizes[1]), need \$N\"))\n    end\n\n    # Mixed precision: the F32 hierarchy hosts the inner error-equation V-cycle.\n    # Allocated here only for standalone calls; repeated solvers (SIMPLE loops)\n    # should pass a shared `hier_f32` exactly like `hier`.\n    if mixed_precision\n        if hier_f32 === nothing\n            hier_f32 = build_mg_hierarchy(N, _mg_eltype_variant(atype, Float32);\n                                          min_size = min_size)\n        else\n            hier_f32.sizes[1] == N ||\n                throw(ArgumentError(\"reused F32 hierarchy is sized \$(hier_f32.sizes[1]), need \$N\"))\n            eltype(hier_f32.u[1]) === Float32 ||\n                throw(ArgumentError(\"hier_f32 must hold Float32 arrays\"))\n        end\n    end\n\n    # Fill the finest RHS at cell centres. Sampling a Function is a host loop into\n    # a host staging array, then copied to the device array (no device scalar\n    # indexing). If `f` is already an array, just copy it.\n    if f isa Function\n        host = Matrix{Float64}(undef, N, N)\n        h = 1.0 / N\n        @inbounds for j in 1:N, i in 1:N\n            x = (i - 0.5) * h\n            y = (j - 0.5) * h\n            host[i, j] = Float64(f(x, y))\n        end\n        copyto!(hier.f[1], host)\n    else\n        size(f) == (N, N) || throw(ArgumentError(\"f array must be N x N\"))\n        copyto!(hier.f[1], f)\n    end\n\n    # For the singular Neumann problem the RHS must be in the range of L\n    # (zero mean). Project it. A Helmholtz shift (sig>0) makes the operator\n    # non-singular, so zero-mean handling is only applied for the pure-Neumann,\n    # sig=0 case (neumann_pin is only set for :neumann bc, which the cavity uses\n    # with sig=0 for the pressure solve). In fixed-cycles mode the projection\n    # is SKIPPED entirely (it is a host-sync reduction at every level of every\n    # cycle): the V-cycle commutes with constant shifts and the caller's RHS is\n    # discretely zero-mean, so the answer differs by a constant only (gauged by\n    # the caller).\n    do_project = neumann_pin && sig == 0.0 && nfixed == 0\n    if do_project\n        _project_zero_mean!(hier.f[1], N, N, kab, hier.scratch[1])\n    end\n\n    # Initial guess: zero, or a caller-supplied warm start (e.g. the previous\n    # outer-iteration solution, which cuts V-cycles markedly in SIMPLE loops).\n    if u0 === nothing\n        _mg_zero!(hier.u[1], N, N, kab)\n    else\n        size(u0) == (N, N) || throw(ArgumentError(\"u0 must be N x N\"))\n        copyto!(hier.u[1], u0)\n    end\n\n    # ---- fixed-cycle mode: static launch sequence, ZERO host syncs ----------\n    if nfixed > 0\n        if mixed_precision\n            # Each fixed \"cycle\" is one F64 defect-correction pass wrapping one\n            # F32 V-cycle — still a static, reduction-free launch sequence\n            # (CUDA-graph-capturable). Zero-mean projections stay skipped (the\n            # defect correction commutes with constant shifts the same way the\n            # plain Neumann V-cycle does; the caller gauges the constant).\n            for _ in 1:nfixed\n                _mg_mixed_cycle!(hier, hier_f32, bcs, kab;\n                                 nu1 = Int(nu1), nu2 = Int(nu2),\n                                 ncoarse = Int(ncoarse), smoother = smoother,\n                                 sigma = sig, project = false)\n            end\n        else\n            for _ in 1:nfixed\n                vcycle!(hier, 1, bcs, kab; nu1 = Int(nu1), nu2 = Int(nu2),\n                        ncoarse = Int(ncoarse), smoother = smoother,\n                        neumann_pin = false, sigma = sig)\n            end\n        end\n        return hier.u[1], nfixed, Float64[]\n    end\n\n    # ---- tolerance-driven mode (legacy, unchanged) --------------------------\n    fnorm = norm(hier.f[1])\n    fnorm == 0 && (fnorm = 1.0)\n\n    resid_history = Float64[]\n    relres, _ = _mg_relresid(hier, bcs, kab; fnorm = fnorm, sigma = sig)\n    push!(resid_history, relres)\n    verbose && @info \"MG start\" N relres\n\n    ncycles = 0\n    for cyc in 1:Int(maxcycles)\n        if mixed_precision\n            _mg_mixed_cycle!(hier, hier_f32, bcs, kab;\n                             nu1 = Int(nu1), nu2 = Int(nu2),\n                             ncoarse = Int(ncoarse), smoother = smoother,\n                             sigma = sig, project = do_project)\n        else\n            vcycle!(hier, 1, bcs, kab; nu1 = Int(nu1), nu2 = Int(nu2),\n                    ncoarse = Int(ncoarse), smoother = smoother,\n                    neumann_pin = do_project, sigma = sig)\n        end\n        ncycles += 1\n        relres, _ = _mg_relresid(hier, bcs, kab; fnorm = fnorm, sigma = sig)\n        push!(resid_history, relres)\n        verbose && @info \"MG cycle\" cyc relres\n        relres <= tol && break\n    end\n\n    return hier.u[1], ncycles, resid_history\nend\n```"), (name = :solve_poisson_mgcg, signature = "function solve_poisson_mgcg(f, N::Integer;", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    solve_poisson_mgcg(f, N; Dirichlet only (SPD). Dirichlet only (SPD). Bonus path; same KA-generic structure.\n\"\"\"\nfunction solve_poisson_mgcg(f, N::Integer;\n                            bc::Symbol = :dirichlet,\n                            backend::LinearSolveBackend = CPUBackendTag(),\n                            backend_ka = _mg_ka_backend(backend),\n                            atype::Type{<:AbstractArray} = Array{Float64},\n                            tol::Real = 1e-10,\n                            maxiters::Integer = 100,\n                            nu1::Integer = 2,\n                            nu2::Integer = 2,\n                            ncoarse::Integer = 50,\n                            smoother::Symbol = :rbgs,\n                            min_size::Integer = 4,\n                            verbose::Bool = false)\n    bc === :dirichlet || throw(ArgumentError(\"MG-CG wrapper is Dirichlet-only (SPD)\"))\n    N = Int(N)\n    kab = backend_ka\n    bcs = (MG_BC_DIRICHLET, MG_BC_DIRICHLET, MG_BC_DIRICHLET, MG_BC_DIRICHLET)\n    invh2 = N^2  # 1/h^2 at finest\n\n    # Hierarchy reused as the preconditioner workspace.\n    hier = build_mg_hierarchy(N, atype; min_size = min_size)\n\n    # CG vectors.\n    x  = atype(undef, N, N); fill!(x, 0.0)\n    b  = atype(undef, N, N)\n    r  = atype(undef, N, N)\n    z  = atype(undef, N, N)\n    p  = atype(undef, N, N)\n    Ap = atype(undef, N, N)\n\n    if f isa Function\n        host = Matrix{Float64}(undef, N, N)\n        h = 1.0 / N\n        @inbounds for j in 1:N, i in 1:N\n            host[i, j] = Float64(f((i - 0.5) * h, (j - 0.5) * h))\n        end\n        copyto!(b, host)\n    else\n        copyto!(b, f)\n    end\n\n    # r = b - A x = b (x=0)\n    copyto!(r, b)\n    bnorm = norm(b); bnorm == 0 && (bnorm = 1.0)\n\n    apply_M!(zout, rin) = begin\n        # One V-cycle preconditioner: solve A z ≈ rin with z0 = 0.\n        copyto!(hier.f[1], rin)\n        _mg_zero!(hier.u[1], N, N, kab)\n        vcycle!(hier, 1, bcs, kab; nu1 = Int(nu1), nu2 = Int(nu2),\n                ncoarse = Int(ncoarse), smoother = smoother, neumann_pin = false,\n                sigma = 0.0)\n        copyto!(zout, hier.u[1])\n    end\n\n    apply_M!(z, r)\n    copyto!(p, z)\n    rz = _mg_dot(r, z)\n\n    resid_history = Float64[norm(r) / bnorm]\n    verbose && @info \"MG-CG start\" resid_history[end]\n\n    niters = 0\n    for it in 1:Int(maxiters)\n        _mg_apply!(Ap, p, invh2, 0.0, bcs, N, N, kab)\n        pAp = _mg_dot(p, Ap)\n        alpha = rz / pAp\n        mg_axpy_kernel!(kab)(x, alpha, p, N, N; ndrange = (N, N))\n        KernelAbstractions.synchronize(kab)\n        mg_axpy_kernel!(kab)(r, -alpha, Ap, N, N; ndrange = (N, N))\n        KernelAbstractions.synchronize(kab)\n        niters += 1\n        relres = norm(r) / bnorm\n        push!(resid_history, relres)\n        verbose && @info \"MG-CG it\" it relres\n        relres <= tol && break\n        apply_M!(z, r)\n        rz_new = _mg_dot(r, z)\n        beta = rz_new / rz\n        mg_xpay_kernel!(kab)(p, z, beta, N, N; ndrange = (N, N))\n        KernelAbstractions.synchronize(kab)\n        rz = rz_new\n    end\n\n    return x, niters, resid_history\nend\n```"), (name = :gdl_divergence_2d!, signature = "function gdl_divergence_2d!(", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    gdl_divergence_2d!(divu, ux, uy, is_solid, dx, dy,\n                       west_bc, east_bc, south_bc, north_bc;\n                       backend=get_backend(divu), sync=true)\n    gdl_divergence_2d!(divu, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                       west_fraction, east_fraction,\n                       south_fraction, north_fraction, cell_fraction,\n                       dx, dy, west_bc, east_bc, south_bc, north_bc; Prefer\n`compute_drag_libb_mei_2d` for quantitative Schäfer-Turek-style\nbenchmarks.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    compute_drag_libb_2d(f_pre, q_wall, Nx, Ny)\n        -> (Fx, Fy)\n\nSimple halfway-BB MEA drag (2·c_q·f_q at the fluid cell). Underestimates\nCd when q_w ≠ 0.5; kept for the old scaffold/test. Prefer\n`compute_drag_libb_mei_2d` for quantitative Schäfer-Turek-style\nbenchmarks.\n\"\"\"\nfunction compute_drag_libb_2d(f_post, q_wall, Nx::Int, Ny::Int)\n    f = Array(f_post)\n    qw = Array(q_wall)\n    cxv = (0, 1, 0, -1,  0, 1, -1, -1,  1)\n    cyv = (0, 0, 1,  0, -1, 1,  1, -1, -1)\n    Fx = 0.0; Fy = 0.0\n    @inbounds for j in 1:Ny, i in 1:Nx\n        for q in 2:9\n            if qw[i, j, q] > 0\n                Fx += 2.0 * Float64(cxv[q]) * Float64(f[i, j, q])\n                Fy += 2.0 * Float64(cyv[q]) * Float64(f[i, j, q])\n            end\n        end\n    end\n    return (Fx = Fx, Fy = Fy)\nend\n```"), (name = :compute_drag_libb_mei_2d, signature = "function compute_drag_libb_mei_2d(f_pre, q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    compute_drag_libb_mei_2d(f_pre, q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y, Nx, Ny)\n        -> (Fx, Fy)\n\nMei-Luo-Shyy 2002 (J. Comput. Phys. 161, 680) momentum-exchange drag\nfor LI-BB. Consistent with the V2 pre-phase Bouzidi substitution: for\neach cut link q on a fluid cell, the force per link per step is\n\n    F_link = c_q · (f_q_pre + f_q̄_bouzidi)\n\nwhere `f_q_pre = f_pre[i,j,q]` (pop q pre-step at the fluid cell,\ni.e. post-coll from the previous step) and `f_q̄_bouzidi` is the\narriving pop computed via the same `_libb_branch` used in the\nkernel's ApplyLiBBPrePhase brick (lag-1 Bouzidi estimate). Reduces to\n`2·c_q·f_q` at q_w = 0.5 stationary, matching the halfway formula.\n\n`f_pre` must be the `f_in` array at step N (= `f_out` from step N-1\nBEFORE the boundary patches of step N are applied; in the driver we\npass the full `f_in` each sampling step). `uw_link_x/y` are the per-\nlink wall-velocity arrays (zero for a stationary cylinder).\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    compute_drag_libb_mei_2d(f_pre, q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y, Nx, Ny)\n        -> (Fx, Fy)\n\nMei-Luo-Shyy 2002 (J. Comput. Phys. 161, 680) momentum-exchange drag\nfor LI-BB. Consistent with the V2 pre-phase Bouzidi substitution: for\neach cut link q on a fluid cell, the force per link per step is\n\n    F_link = c_q · (f_q_pre + f_q̄_bouzidi)\n\nwhere `f_q_pre = f_pre[i,j,q]` (pop q pre-step at the fluid cell,\ni.e. post-coll from the previous step) and `f_q̄_bouzidi` is the\narriving pop computed via the same `_libb_branch` used in the\nkernel's ApplyLiBBPrePhase brick (lag-1 Bouzidi estimate). Reduces to\n`2·c_q·f_q` at q_w = 0.5 stationary, matching the halfway formula.\n\n`f_pre` must be the `f_in` array at step N (= `f_out` from step N-1\nBEFORE the boundary patches of step N are applied; in the driver we\npass the full `f_in` each sampling step). `uw_link_x/y` are the per-\nlink wall-velocity arrays (zero for a stationary cylinder).\n\"\"\"\nfunction compute_drag_libb_mei_2d(f_pre, q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y,\n                                    Nx::Int, Ny::Int)\n    backend = KernelAbstractions.get_backend(f_pre)\n    if backend isa KernelAbstractions.CPU\n        return _compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_host(f_pre, q_wall, uw_link_x,\n                                                uw_link_y, Nx, Ny)\n    else\n        return _compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_gpu_cached(f_pre, q_wall, uw_link_x,\n                                                      uw_link_y, Nx, Ny)\n    end\nend\n```"), (name = :rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_2d!, signature = "function rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_2d!(f_out, f_in, u_profile, ρ_out::Real,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_2d!(f_out, f_in, u_profile, ρ_out, ν, Nx, Ny)\n\nLegacy wrapper for the hardcoded (ZouHe-velocity west + ZouHe-pressure\neast) rebuild. Prefer the modular `apply_bc_rebuild_2d!(f_out, f_in,\nBCSpec2D(west=ZouHeVelocity(u_profile), east=ZouHePressure(ρ_out)),\nν, Nx, Ny)` in new code — it decouples BC choice from the driver.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_2d!(f_out, f_in, u_profile, ρ_out, ν, Nx, Ny)\n\nLegacy wrapper for the hardcoded (ZouHe-velocity west + ZouHe-pressure\neast) rebuild. Prefer the modular `apply_bc_rebuild_2d!(f_out, f_in,\nBCSpec2D(west=ZouHeVelocity(u_profile), east=ZouHePressure(ρ_out)),\nν, Nx, Ny)` in new code — it decouples BC choice from the driver.\n\"\"\"\nfunction rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_2d!(f_out, f_in, u_profile, ρ_out::Real,\n                                        ν::Real, Nx::Int, Ny::Int)\n    bc = BCSpec2D(; west = ZouHeVelocity(u_profile),\n                    east = ZouHePressure(eltype(f_out)(ρ_out)))\n    apply_bc_rebuild_2d!(f_out, f_in, bc, ν, Nx, Ny)\nend\n```"), (name = :rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_3d!, signature = "function rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_3d!(f_out, f_in, u_in::Real, ρ_out::Real,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_3d!(f_out, f_in, u_in, ρ_out, ν, Nx, Ny, Nz)\n\nLegacy wrapper for the hardcoded 3D (ZouHe-velocity west + ZouHe-pressure\neast) rebuild. Prefer the modular `apply_bc_rebuild_3d!(f_out, f_in,\nBCSpec3D(west=ZouHeVelocity(fill(u_in, Ny)), east=ZouHePressure(ρ_out)),\nν, Nx, Ny, Nz)` in new code.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_3d!(f_out, f_in, u_in, ρ_out, ν, Nx, Ny, Nz)\n\nLegacy wrapper for the hardcoded 3D (ZouHe-velocity west + ZouHe-pressure\neast) rebuild. Prefer the modular `apply_bc_rebuild_3d!(f_out, f_in,\nBCSpec3D(west=ZouHeVelocity(fill(u_in, Ny)), east=ZouHePressure(ρ_out)),\nν, Nx, Ny, Nz)` in new code.\n\"\"\"\nfunction rebuild_inlet_outlet_libb_3d!(f_out, f_in, u_in::Real, ρ_out::Real,\n                                         ν::Real, Nx::Int, Ny::Int, Nz::Int)\n    T = eltype(f_out)\n    # Build a device profile matching backend for the ZouHeVelocity BC.\n    backend = KernelAbstractions.get_backend(f_out)\n    prof = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, T, Ny)\n    fill!(prof, T(u_in))\n    bc = BCSpec3D(; west = ZouHeVelocity(prof),\n                    east = ZouHePressure(T(ρ_out)))\n    apply_bc_rebuild_3d!(f_out, f_in, bc, ν, Nx, Ny, Nz)\n    return\n    return nothing\nend\n```"), (name = :AbstractBC, signature = "", docstring = "", source_excerpt = ""), (name = :HalfwayBB, signature = "struct HalfwayBB <: AbstractBC end", docstring = "\"Kernel-fallback halfway bounce-back. Tangential velocity is assumed zero.\n\nFor a 2D x-face with a parabolic channel profile, pass the discrete\n`u(y)` array. For uniform inflow, `fill(T(u_in), Ny)`.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    ZouHeVelocity(profile)\n\nZou-He velocity boundary condition. `profile` is a device array of\nlength N (N = Ny for x-faces, Nx for y-faces, Nx·Nz or similar for\nz-faces in 3D) giving the normal-into-domain velocity at each cell on\nthe face. Tangential velocity is assumed zero.\n\nFor a 2D x-face with a parabolic channel profile, pass the discrete\n`u(y)` array. Defaults are\n`HalfwayBB` (kernel-fallback) so only set the faces that differ.\n\"\"\"\nstruct BCSpec2D{W<:AbstractBC, E<:AbstractBC, S<:AbstractBC, N<:AbstractBC}\n    west::W\n    east::E\n    south::S\n    north::N\nend\n```"), (name = :BCSpec3D, signature = "struct BCSpec3D{W<:AbstractBC, E<:AbstractBC, S<:AbstractBC,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    BCSpec3D(; west, east, south, north, bottom, top)\n\nPer-face BC specification for a 3D rectangular box domain.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    BCSpec3D(; west, east, south, north, bottom, top)\n\nPer-face BC specification for a 3D rectangular box domain.\n\"\"\"\nstruct BCSpec3D{W<:AbstractBC, E<:AbstractBC, S<:AbstractBC,\n                 N<:AbstractBC, B<:AbstractBC, T<:AbstractBC}\n    west::W; east::E; south::S; north::N; bottom::B; top::T\nend\n```"), (name = :compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_gpu!, signature = "function compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_gpu!(Fx_link, Fy_link, links::CutLinkList,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_gpu!(Fx_link, Fy_link, links::CutLinkList,\n                                     f, uw_x, uw_y, Nx, Ny)\n\nCompute each cut link's Fx, Fy contribution into dense device arrays\n`Fx_link`, `Fy_link` (length = `links.Nlinks`). The caller sums on host with\n`sum(Array(Fx_link))` — transferring at most a few kilobytes.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_gpu!(Fx_link, Fy_link, links::CutLinkList,\n                                     f, uw_x, uw_y, Nx, Ny)\n\nCompute each cut link's Fx, Fy contribution into dense device arrays\n`Fx_link`, `Fy_link` (length = `links.Nlinks`). No atomic operations;\neach thread writes its own slot. The caller sums on host with\n`sum(Array(Fx_link))` — transferring at most a few kilobytes.\n\"\"\"\nfunction compute_drag_libb_mei_2d_gpu!(Fx_link, Fy_link, links::CutLinkList,\n                                         f, uw_x, uw_y,\n                                         Nx::Integer, Ny::Integer)\n    # Skip kernel launch for empty link list — KernelAbstractions on CUDA\n    # with ndrange=(0,) triggers an integer division error in the\n    # workgroup-size computation. An empty list can arise in multi-block\n    # setups where some blocks do not contain any cut cells (the cylinder\n    # sits entirely in another block).\n    links.Nlinks == 0 && return nothing\n    backend = KernelAbstractions.get_backend(f)\n    _drag_mei_2d_list_kernel!(backend)(Fx_link, Fy_link,\n                                         links.list_i, links.list_j,\n                                         links.list_q, links.list_qw,\n                                         f, uw_x, uw_y, Nx, Ny;\n                                         ndrange=(links.Nlinks,))\n    return nothing\nend\n```"), (name = :compute_drag_libb_3d_gpu!, signature = "function compute_drag_libb_3d_gpu!(Fx_link, Fy_link, Fz_link,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    compute_drag_libb_3d_gpu!(Fx_link, Fy_link, Fz_link,\n                                links::CutLinkList3D, f, Nx, Ny, Nz)\n\nGPU halfway-BB Ladd drag on cut-link list (no atomics). Built once via `build_cut_link_list_2d(q_wall_h)`\non host, copied to the target backend.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    CutLinkList{AT}\n\nCompact device-side representation of the cut links flagged by\n`q_wall > 0` — `list_i`, `list_j`, `list_q`, `list_qw` are parallel\narrays of length `Nlinks`. Built once via `build_cut_link_list_2d(q_wall_h)`\non host, copied to the target backend.\n\"\"\"\nstruct CutLinkList{IT<:AbstractVector{Int32}, WT<:AbstractVector}\n    list_i::IT\n    list_j::IT\n    list_q::IT\n    list_qw::WT\n    Nlinks::Int\nend\n```"), (name = :CutLinkList3D, signature = "struct CutLinkList3D{IT<:AbstractVector{Int32}, WT<:AbstractVector}", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    CutLinkList3D\n\nPublic type or module in the kernel-level LBM operation.\nConstruct or dispatch on this type according to the field layout and methods defined below.\n\n```julia\nusing Kraken\n\nKraken.CutLinkList3D\n```\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    CutLinkList3D\n\nPublic type or module in the kernel-level LBM operation.\nConstruct or dispatch on this type according to the field layout and methods defined below.\n\n```julia\nusing Kraken\n\nKraken.CutLinkList3D\n```\n\"\"\"\nstruct CutLinkList3D{IT<:AbstractVector{Int32}, WT<:AbstractVector}\n    list_i::IT; list_j::IT; list_k::IT; list_q::IT\n    list_qw::WT\n    Nlinks::Int\nend\n```"), (name = :build_cut_link_list_2d, signature = "function build_cut_link_list_2d(q_wall_h::AbstractArray{T,3}; backend=CPU()) where {T}", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    build_cut_link_list_2d(q_wall_h::Array{T,3}; backend=CPU())\n                          -> CutLinkList\n\nScan a host `q_wall_h[Nx, Ny, 9]` array, collect the coordinates of\nevery cut link, and upload to `backend`. O(Nx·Ny) once at setup.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    build_cut_link_list_2d(q_wall_h::Array{T,3}; backend=CPU())\n                          -> CutLinkList\n\nScan a host `q_wall_h[Nx, Ny, 9]` array, collect the coordinates of\nevery cut link, and upload to `backend`. O(Nx·Ny) once at setup.\n\"\"\"\nfunction build_cut_link_list_2d(q_wall_h::AbstractArray{T,3}; backend=CPU()) where {T}\n    Nx, Ny, _ = size(q_wall_h)\n    is_h = Int32[]; js_h = Int32[]; qs_h = Int32[]; qws_h = T[]\n    @inbounds for j in 1:Ny, i in 1:Nx, q in 2:9\n        if q_wall_h[i,j,q] > 0\n            push!(is_h, i); push!(js_h, j); push!(qs_h, q)\n            push!(qws_h, q_wall_h[i,j,q])\n        end\n    end\n    N = length(is_h)\n    li = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lj = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lq = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lw = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, T,      N)\n    copyto!(li, is_h); copyto!(lj, js_h)\n    copyto!(lq, qs_h); copyto!(lw, qws_h)\n    return CutLinkList(li, lj, lq, lw, N)\nend\n```"), (name = :build_cut_link_list_3d, signature = "function build_cut_link_list_3d(q_wall_h::AbstractArray{T,4}; backend=CPU()) where {T}", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    build_cut_link_list_3d(q_wall_h::AbstractArray{T,4}; backend=CPU()) where {T}\n\nPublic function in the kernel-level LBM operation.\nSee the method definition below for argument requirements, array layout, and backend expectations.\n\n```julia\nusing Kraken\n\nmethods(Kraken.build_cut_link_list_3d)\n```\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    build_cut_link_list_3d(q_wall_h::AbstractArray{T,4}; backend=CPU()) where {T}\n\nPublic function in the kernel-level LBM operation.\nSee the method definition below for argument requirements, array layout, and backend expectations.\n\n```julia\nusing Kraken\n\nmethods(Kraken.build_cut_link_list_3d)\n```\n\"\"\"\nfunction build_cut_link_list_3d(q_wall_h::AbstractArray{T,4}; backend=CPU()) where {T}\n    Nx, Ny, Nz, _ = size(q_wall_h)\n    is_h = Int32[]; js_h = Int32[]; ks_h = Int32[]; qs_h = Int32[]; qws_h = T[]\n    @inbounds for k in 1:Nz, j in 1:Ny, i in 1:Nx, q in 2:19\n        if q_wall_h[i,j,k,q] > 0\n            push!(is_h, i); push!(js_h, j); push!(ks_h, k); push!(qs_h, q)\n            push!(qws_h, q_wall_h[i,j,k,q])\n        end\n    end\n    N = length(is_h)\n    li = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lj = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lk = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lq = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, Int32, N)\n    lw = KernelAbstractions.allocate(backend, T,      N)\n    copyto!(li, is_h); copyto!(lj, js_h); copyto!(lk, ks_h)\n    copyto!(lq, qs_h); copyto!(lw, qws_h)\n    return CutLinkList3D(li, lj, lk, lq, lw, N)\nend\n```"), (name = :compute_temperature_2d!, signature = "function compute_temperature_2d!(Temp, g)", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    compute_temperature_2d!(Temp, g)\n\nPublic function in the kernel-level LBM operation.\nSee the method definition below for argument requirements, array layout, and backend expectations. Uses Λ = 3/16 by default (Ginzburg-magic bounce-back).\nPass `Λ = Inf` (or any large value) for pure BGK behaviour —\n`s_plus → 0` yields `a = s_minus/2`, which is NOT BGK. To recover BGK\nexactly, pass `Λ = (1/s − 0.5)²` with s = 1/(3ν+0.5), or equivalently\ncall `fused_bgk_step!`.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    fused_trt_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid, Nx, Ny, ν; Λ=3/16)\n\nSingle fused GPU kernel: stream + halfway bounce-back + TRT collide +\nmacroscopic. Uses Λ = 3/16 by default (Ginzburg-magic bounce-back).\nPass `Λ = Inf` (or any large value) for pure BGK behaviour —\n`s_plus → 0` yields `a = s_minus/2`, which is NOT BGK. To recover BGK\nexactly, pass `Λ = (1/s − 0.5)²` with s = 1/(3ν+0.5), or equivalently\ncall `fused_bgk_step!`.\n\"\"\"\nfunction fused_trt_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid, Nx, Ny, ν;\n                          Λ::Real=3/16)\n    backend = KernelAbstractions.get_backend(f_in)\n    ET = eltype(f_in)\n    s_plus, s_minus = trt_rates(ν; Λ=Λ)\n    kernel! = fused_trt_step_kernel!(backend)\n    kernel!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid, Nx, Ny,\n            ET(s_plus), ET(s_minus); ndrange=(Nx, Ny))\nend\n```"), (name = :trt_rates, signature = "function trt_rates(ν::Real; Λ::Real=3/16)", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    trt_rates(ν; Λ=3/16) -> (s_plus, s_minus)\n\nCompute the TRT relaxation rates from kinematic viscosity `ν` and the\nmagic parameter `Λ`. Following Ginzburg & d'Humières 2003 (PRE 68,\n066614) and Krüger et al. 2017 (ch. 10.5):\n\n- `s_plus` — rate of the SYMMETRIC (even) mode (f_q + f_q̄)/2. Sets\n  the kinematic shear viscosity via `ν = (1/s_plus − 1/2) / 3`, so\n  `s_plus = 1/(3ν + 1/2)`.\n- `s_minus` — rate of the ANTISYMMETRIC (odd) mode (f_q − f_q̄)/2.\n  Set by the magic parameter via `(1/s_plus − 1/2)(1/s_minus − 1/2) = Λ`,\n  so `s_minus = 1/(Λ/(3ν) + 1/2)`.\n\nThe fused TRT/BGK collide in this file applies `s_plus` to the even\nmode and `s_minus` to the odd mode — consistent with this convention.\nDefault `Λ = 3/16` makes the halfway bounce-back error\nviscosity-independent (Ginzburg & d'Humières 2003).\n\nHistorical note: commits before 2026-04-15 returned the two rates with\nlabels swapped (`s_plus` set from Λ, `s_minus` from ν). The collide\nformula then applied the Λ-derived rate to the even mode, giving an\neffective viscosity `ν_eff = Λ/(9ν)` ≈ 13×ν at Λ=3/16, ν=0.04. This\ninflated the real Re by ~13× and silently over-dragged every\nbenchmark that relied on `trt_rates`. Fixed here.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    trt_rates(ν; Λ=3/16) -> (s_plus, s_minus)\n\nCompute the TRT relaxation rates from kinematic viscosity `ν` and the\nmagic parameter `Λ`. Following Ginzburg & d'Humières 2003 (PRE 68,\n066614) and Krüger et al. 2017 (ch. 10.5):\n\n- `s_plus` — rate of the SYMMETRIC (even) mode (f_q + f_q̄)/2. Sets\n  the kinematic shear viscosity via `ν = (1/s_plus − 1/2) / 3`, so\n  `s_plus = 1/(3ν + 1/2)`.\n- `s_minus` — rate of the ANTISYMMETRIC (odd) mode (f_q − f_q̄)/2.\n  Set by the magic parameter via `(1/s_plus − 1/2)(1/s_minus − 1/2) = Λ`,\n  so `s_minus = 1/(Λ/(3ν) + 1/2)`.\n\nThe fused TRT/BGK collide in this file applies `s_plus` to the even\nmode and `s_minus` to the odd mode — consistent with this convention.\nDefault `Λ = 3/16` makes the halfway bounce-back error\nviscosity-independent (Ginzburg & d'Humières 2003).\n\nHistorical note: commits before 2026-04-15 returned the two rates with\nlabels swapped (`s_plus` set from Λ, `s_minus` from ν). The collide\nformula then applied the Λ-derived rate to the even mode, giving an\neffective viscosity `ν_eff = Λ/(9ν)` ≈ 13×ν at Λ=3/16, ν=0.04. This\ninflated the real Re by ~13× and silently over-dragged every\nbenchmark that relied on `trt_rates`. Fixed here.\n\"\"\"\nfunction trt_rates(ν::Real; Λ::Real=3/16)\n    s_plus  = 1.0 / (3ν + 0.5)\n    s_minus = 1.0 / (Λ / (3ν) + 0.5)\n    return s_plus, s_minus\nend\n```"), (name = :fused_trt_libb_step!, signature = "function fused_trt_libb_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    fused_trt_libb_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                          q_wall, uw_x, uw_y, Nx, Ny, ν; Λ=3/16)\n\nFused GPU step: pull-stream + halfway BB on domain edges + TRT\ncollision + interpolated bounce-back (Bouzidi) on flagged cut links.\n`q_wall[i,j,q]` holds the wall-cut fraction per link (0 if no\ncrossing, (0,1] otherwise). `uw_x`, `uw_y` are per-cell prescribed\nwall velocities; pass zero arrays for stationary walls.\n\nSets the symmetric rate via TRT magic `Λ = 3/16` by default, making\nthe bounce-back error viscosity-independent (Ginzburg 2003). Pass a\ndifferent `Λ` for other choices.\n\"\"\"", source_excerpt = "```julia\n\"\"\"\n    fused_trt_libb_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                          q_wall, uw_x, uw_y, Nx, Ny, ν; Λ=3/16)\n\nFused GPU step: pull-stream + halfway BB on domain edges + TRT\ncollision + interpolated bounce-back (Bouzidi) on flagged cut links.\n`q_wall[i,j,q]` holds the wall-cut fraction per link (0 if no\ncrossing, (0,1] otherwise). `uw_x`, `uw_y` are per-cell prescribed\nwall velocities; pass zero arrays for stationary walls.\n\nSets the symmetric rate via TRT magic `Λ = 3/16` by default, making\nthe bounce-back error viscosity-independent (Ginzburg 2003). Pass a\ndifferent `Λ` for other choices.\n\"\"\"\nfunction fused_trt_libb_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                               q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y,\n                               Nx, Ny, ν; Λ::Real=3/16)\n    backend = KernelAbstractions.get_backend(f_in)\n    ET = eltype(f_in)\n    s_plus, s_minus = trt_rates(ν; Λ=Λ)\n    kernel! = fused_trt_libb_step_kernel!(backend)\n    kernel!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n            q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y,\n            Nx, Ny, ET(s_plus), ET(s_minus);\n            ndrange=(Nx, Ny))\nend\n```"), (name = :fused_trt_libb_v2_step!, signature = "function fused_trt_libb_v2_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    fused_trt_libb_v2_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                             q_wall, uw_x, uw_y, Nx, Ny, ν; Λ=3/16)\n\nRefactored TRT + LI-BB step that fixes the double-BC bug of\n`fused_trt_libb_step!`. Λ=3/16, source_scale=1)\n\nExperimental LI-BB V2 step with the polymer Hermite stress source fused into\nthe TRT collision. `source_scale=1` gives the local Liu/Yu in-collision\namplitude; `source_scale=1/(1-s_plus/2)` gives the standalone CE-corrected\namplitude used by the post-collision source.\n\"\"\"\nfunction fused_trt_libb_v2_hermite_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                                           q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y,\n                                           tau_p_xx, tau_p_xy, tau_p_yy,\n                                           Nx, Ny, ν; Λ::Real=3/16,\n                                           source_scale::Real=1,\n                                           source_on_cutlinks::Bool=true)\n    backend = KernelAbstractions.get_backend(f_in)\n    ET = eltype(f_in)\n    s_plus, s_minus = trt_rates(ν; Λ=Λ)\n    kernel! = build_lbm_kernel(backend, _TRT_LIBB_V2_HERMITE_SPEC)\n    kernel!(f_out, ρ, ux, uy, f_in, is_solid,\n            q_wall, uw_link_x, uw_link_y,\n            Nx, Ny, ET(s_plus), ET(s_minus),\n            tau_p_xx, tau_p_xy, tau_p_yy,\n            ET(source_scale), source_on_cutlinks;\n            ndrange=(Nx, Ny))\nend\n```"), (name = :fused_trt_libb_v2_guo_field_step!, signature = "function fused_trt_libb_v2_guo_field_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,", docstring = "\"\"\"\n    fused_trt_libb_v2_guo_field_step!(f_out, f_in, ρ, ux, uy, is_solid,\n                                       q_wall, uw_x, uw_y, Fx, Fy,\n                                       Nx, Ny, ν;
